title: High-Fiber Diet and Blood Pressure Study
headline: Eating more fiber lowers blood pressure
summary: In this large trial, researchers randomly assigned 1,240 adults with high blood pressure to either a high-fiber diet or their usual diet for 12 weeks. Those eating more fiber saw their blood pressure drop by about 8 points on average. This is strong evidence because participants were randomly assigned to groups and the large sample size provides reliable estimates.
intervention_description: Participants consumed 30 grams of dietary fiber daily through whole grains fruits and vegetables

title: Walking Program for Cardiovascular Health
headline: Walking 30 minutes a day improves heart health
summary: In this large trial, researchers randomly assigned 860 people who don't exercise to either start walking or continue their usual routine for 12 weeks. Those who walked 30 minutes a day, five days a week, showed clear improvements in cardiovascular fitness. This is strong evidence because participants were randomly assigned and the large sample size provides reliable estimates.
intervention_description: 30 minutes of brisk walking 5 days per week for 12 weeks

title: Mediterranean Diet and HbA1c in Type 2 Diabetes
headline: Mediterranean diet helps control blood sugar in diabetics
summary: In this large trial, researchers randomly assigned 520 adults with type 2 diabetes to follow either a Mediterranean diet or standard dietary advice for 6 months. Those eating Mediterranean style saw their blood sugar control improve noticeably. This is strong evidence because participants were randomly assigned to groups and the large sample size provides reliable estimates.
intervention_description: Structured Mediterranean diet with olive oil nuts fish and vegetables

title: Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction for Anxiety
headline: Mindfulness training reduces anxiety
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 280 adults with anxiety to either an 8-week mindfulness program or a waiting list. Those who learned mindfulness techniques showed much less anxiety afterward. This is strong evidence because participants were randomly assigned to groups, which helps rule out other explanations for the difference.
intervention_description: 8-week MBSR program with weekly 2.5-hour sessions and daily home practice
population: ages 25 to 55 with generalized anxiety disorder

title: Resistance Training for Older Adults
headline: Strength training helps older adults stay mobile
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 340 adults over 65 to either a 16-week strength training program or a stretching routine. Those who did strength training had noticeably stronger legs and could walk faster. This is strong evidence because participants were randomly assigned to groups, which helps rule out other explanations for the difference.
intervention_description: 16-week program with twice-weekly supervised resistance exercises

title: Probiotic Supplementation and Gut Health
headline: Probiotics may help with digestive discomfort
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 180 adults with irritable bowel syndrome to take either a probiotic pill or a placebo for 8 weeks. Those taking probiotics reported less bloating and stomach pain. This is fairly strong evidence because participants were randomly assigned and didn't know which pill they got.
intervention_description: Daily capsule containing Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium strains
population: ages 30 to 60 with irritable bowel syndrome

title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia
headline: CBT works better than sleep tips for insomnia
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 196 adults with chronic sleep problems to either a 6-week therapy program or basic sleep education. Those who got therapy slept much better afterward. This is strong evidence because participants were randomly assigned to groups, which helps rule out other explanations for the difference.
intervention_description: 6-week CBT-I program with weekly sessions covering sleep restriction stimulus control and cognitive restructuring

title: Yoga for Low Back Pain
headline: Yoga helps with chronic back pain
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 220 adults with ongoing back pain to either take yoga classes or continue their usual care for 12 weeks. Those who did yoga reported less pain and moved around more easily. This is fairly strong evidence because participants were randomly assigned to groups.
intervention_description: 12-week program with twice-weekly 75-minute Hatha yoga classes
population: ages 25 to 65 with chronic low back pain

title: Cervical Cancer Screening with HPV Self-Collection
headline: At-home HPV test kits get more women screened for cervical cancer
summary: In this large trial, researchers randomly assigned 2,474 women who were overdue for cervical cancer screening to receive either a phone reminder alone or a phone reminder plus a mail-in test kit. Women who got the kit were more than twice as likely to complete screening. This is strong evidence because participants were randomly assigned and the large sample size provides reliable estimates.
intervention_description: Participants receive a mailed kit to self-collect a sample at home and return it for testing
population: ages 30 to 65 women overdue for screening

title: DASH Diet for Hypertension
headline: The DASH diet lowers blood pressure significantly
summary: In this large trial, researchers randomly assigned 940 adults with high blood pressure to either the DASH diet or a typical American diet for 8 weeks. Those on DASH saw their blood pressure drop substantially. The DASH diet emphasizes fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and low-fat dairy while limiting sodium. This is strong evidence with a large sample.
intervention_description: Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension emphasizing fruits vegetables whole grains low-fat dairy

title: High-Intensity Interval Training vs Moderate Exercise
headline: Short bursts of intense exercise improve fitness as much as longer moderate workouts
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 420 adults to either high-intensity interval training or traditional moderate exercise for 12 weeks. Both groups improved similarly, but HIIT took less time. This shows you can get similar benefits with shorter, harder workouts. Strong evidence from a well-designed study.
intervention_description: 20-minute sessions with alternating 1-minute high-intensity and 2-minute recovery periods

title: Sodium Reduction and Blood Pressure
headline: Cutting back on salt lowers blood pressure
summary: In this large trial, researchers randomly assigned 780 adults to either a reduced sodium diet or their usual diet for 4 weeks. Those eating less salt had noticeably lower blood pressure. The effect was larger in people who already had high blood pressure. This is strong evidence that salt reduction helps.
intervention_description: Daily sodium intake limited to 1500mg compared to typical 3400mg

title: Exercise for Depression
headline: Regular exercise reduces depression symptoms
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 310 adults with moderate depression to either supervised exercise or a waiting list for 12 weeks. Those who exercised showed significant improvement in depression scores. Exercise was about as effective as medication for moderate depression. Strong evidence that exercise helps mood.
intervention_description: Three 45-minute sessions per week of moderate aerobic exercise

title: Whole Grains and Heart Disease Risk
headline: Eating whole grains improves cholesterol levels
summary: In this large trial, researchers randomly assigned 640 adults to eat either whole grain or refined grain products for 16 weeks. Those eating whole grains had better cholesterol levels. Their LDL cholesterol dropped while HDL stayed the same. Strong evidence that whole grains help heart health.
intervention_description: At least 3 servings of whole grains daily replacing refined grains

title: Tai Chi for Fall Prevention in Elderly
headline: Tai Chi reduces falls in older adults
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 580 adults over 70 to either Tai Chi classes or a stretching program for 24 weeks. Those doing Tai Chi had significantly fewer falls. The slow, controlled movements improved balance and confidence. Strong evidence that Tai Chi helps prevent falls.
intervention_description: Twice-weekly 60-minute Tai Chi classes for 24 weeks
population: ages 70 and older at risk for falls

title: Plant-Based Diet and Weight Loss
headline: Switching to a plant-based diet helps with weight loss
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 380 overweight adults to either a plant-based diet or continue their usual diet for 16 weeks. Those eating plant-based lost significantly more weight without counting calories. They also had better cholesterol and blood sugar levels. Strong evidence that plant-based eating helps weight management.
intervention_description: Low-fat vegan diet with no calorie restriction focusing on whole plant foods

title: Sleep Duration and Metabolic Health
headline: Getting 7-8 hours of sleep improves blood sugar control
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 260 adults who regularly slept less than 6 hours to either extend their sleep or maintain their usual schedule for 8 weeks. Those who slept more had better blood sugar control and felt less hungry during the day. Strong evidence that sleep duration affects metabolism.
intervention_description: Participants extended sleep to 7-8 hours per night with coaching support
population: ages 30 to 60 with short sleep duration

title: Swimming for Joint Pain
headline: Swimming reduces pain in people with arthritis
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 290 adults with osteoarthritis to either a swimming program or land-based exercises for 12 weeks. Both groups improved, but swimmers had less pain and better joint function. Swimming puts less stress on joints while building strength. Strong evidence for swimming with arthritis.
intervention_description: Three 45-minute pool sessions per week with structured exercises

title: Intermittent Fasting vs Daily Calorie Restriction
headline: Time-restricted eating works as well as traditional dieting for weight loss
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 420 overweight adults to either intermittent fasting or daily calorie restriction for 12 months. Both groups lost similar amounts of weight. This suggests time-restricted eating is a valid alternative for people who prefer it, but it's not more effective than traditional calorie counting.
intervention_description: 16:8 time-restricted eating with food consumed within an 8-hour window

title: Meditation for Chronic Pain
headline: Regular meditation reduces chronic pain perception
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 240 adults with chronic pain to either an 8-week meditation program or a support group. Those who meditated reported less pain and needed less pain medication. Meditation doesn't eliminate pain but changes how the brain processes it. Strong evidence for mind-body approaches.
intervention_description: 8-week program with daily 20-minute guided meditation sessions

title: Balance Training Prevents Falls
headline: Simple balance exercises reduce falls in older adults
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 720 adults over 65 to either balance training or usual activities for 12 months. Those doing balance exercises had 40% fewer falls. The exercises were simple enough to do at home. Strong evidence that regular balance practice protects against falls.
intervention_description: Daily 15-minute balance exercise program with progressive difficulty

title: Omega-3 Rich Fish Diet and Inflammation
headline: Eating fatty fish twice a week reduces inflammation markers
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 340 adults with elevated inflammation to either eat fatty fish twice weekly or continue their usual diet for 8 weeks. Fish eaters had lower inflammation markers. Note that this tested actual fish, not fish oil supplements, which show weaker effects. Strong evidence for fish consumption.
intervention_description: At least 2 servings per week of salmon mackerel or sardines

title: Smoking Cessation with Counseling Plus Medication
headline: Combining counseling with medication works best for quitting smoking
summary: In this large trial, researchers randomly assigned 1,120 smokers to either counseling plus medication, medication alone, counseling alone, or placebo. The combination group had the highest quit rates at 6 months. Neither approach alone was as effective. Strong evidence for combined treatment.
intervention_description: Weekly counseling sessions combined with varenicline medication

title: Aerobic Exercise Improves Memory
headline: Regular cardio exercise improves memory in older adults
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 390 healthy older adults to either aerobic exercise or stretching for 12 months. Those doing cardio showed better memory performance and larger hippocampus volume on brain scans. Strong evidence that exercise protects brain health with age.
intervention_description: Three 40-minute sessions of moderate walking per week

title: Reducing Ultra-Processed Foods Improves Health
headline: Cutting ultra-processed foods leads to weight loss and better health
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 280 adults to either reduce ultra-processed food intake or continue their usual diet for 4 weeks. Those cutting processed foods lost weight and had lower blood pressure despite no calorie restriction. They naturally ate about 500 fewer calories per day. Strong evidence against ultra-processed foods.
intervention_description: Minimally processed foods replacing ultra-processed options

title: Light Therapy for Seasonal Depression
headline: Light boxes help with winter depression
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 180 adults with seasonal depression to either bright light therapy or dim placebo light for 6 weeks. Those using bright light showed significant mood improvement. Light therapy works as well as medication for seasonal depression. Strong evidence for this non-drug approach.
intervention_description: 30 minutes of 10000 lux bright light each morning
population: ages 20 to 65 with seasonal affective disorder

title: Strength Training Helps Diabetes
headline: Weight lifting improves blood sugar control in diabetics
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 310 adults with type 2 diabetes to either strength training or usual care for 16 weeks. Those lifting weights had better blood sugar control and needed less medication. Strength training was as effective as some diabetes drugs. Strong evidence for resistance exercise in diabetes.
intervention_description: Twice-weekly supervised weight training sessions

title: Protein at Breakfast Helps Weight Control
headline: Eating protein at breakfast reduces hunger throughout the day
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 240 overweight adults to either a high-protein breakfast or usual breakfast for 12 weeks. Those eating more protein at breakfast felt less hungry and snacked less throughout the day. They lost more weight without trying to diet. Strong evidence for breakfast protein.
intervention_description: Breakfast containing at least 30g protein from eggs dairy or lean meat

title: Group Exercise Reduces Loneliness
headline: Exercising with others improves mental health in isolated seniors
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 280 lonely older adults to either group exercise classes or home exercises for 12 weeks. Those in group classes reported less loneliness and depression. The social aspect mattered as much as the exercise itself. Strong evidence that social exercise helps mental health.
intervention_description: Twice-weekly 60-minute group fitness classes

title: Nuts Lower Heart Disease Risk
headline: Eating nuts daily improves cholesterol levels
summary: In this large trial, researchers randomly assigned 580 adults at cardiovascular risk to either eat 30g of mixed nuts daily or avoid nuts for 12 weeks. Nut eaters had better cholesterol levels and lower inflammation. Nuts are calorie-dense but don't cause weight gain when replacing other snacks. Strong evidence for nut consumption.
intervention_description: 30 grams of mixed unsalted nuts daily

title: Walking Speed Training Helps Mobility
headline: Practicing walking faster improves mobility in older adults
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 340 older adults with slow walking speed to either speed training or usual walking for 12 weeks. Those who practiced walking faster improved their speed and could walk farther. This simple intervention helps maintain independence. Strong evidence for gait training.
intervention_description: Structured practice walking at progressively faster speeds
population: ages 70 and older with slow gait

title: Fermented Foods Improve Gut Health
headline: Eating fermented foods increases gut bacteria diversity
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 180 healthy adults to either eat fermented foods daily or increase fiber for 10 weeks. Those eating fermented foods had more diverse gut bacteria and lower inflammation markers. Fermented foods may be more effective than fiber alone for gut health. Strong evidence for fermented foods.
intervention_description: 6 servings daily of yogurt kefir kimchi or other fermented foods

title: Cold Water Swimming Boosts Mood
headline: Regular cold water swimming reduces depression
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 220 adults with mild depression to either cold water swimming or a waiting list for 8 weeks. Swimmers reported significant mood improvements. The cold exposure triggers endorphin release. This is strong evidence, though not everyone can tolerate cold water.
intervention_description: Twice-weekly 10-minute swims in cold open water with gradual adaptation

title: Cycling to Work Reduces Heart Disease Risk
headline: Bike commuting improves cardiovascular health
summary: In this large trial, researchers randomly assigned 680 sedentary workers to either start cycling to work or continue their usual commute for 6 months. Cyclists had better fitness, lower blood pressure, and lost weight. Active commuting is an easy way to add exercise to daily life. Strong evidence for bike commuting.
intervention_description: Cycling to work at least 3 days per week

title: Legumes Help Blood Sugar Control
headline: Eating beans and lentils daily helps manage blood sugar
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 320 adults with prediabetes to either add legumes to their diet or follow usual nutrition advice for 12 weeks. Those eating beans and lentils daily had better blood sugar control. Legumes are high in fiber and protein with low glycemic impact. Strong evidence for legume consumption.
intervention_description: One cup of cooked beans lentils or chickpeas daily

title: Nature Exposure Reduces Stress
headline: Spending time in nature lowers stress hormones
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 260 stressed adults to either spend 20 minutes in nature or an urban environment three times weekly for 8 weeks. Those in nature had lower cortisol levels and reported less stress. Even brief nature exposure has measurable benefits. Strong evidence for nature as medicine.
intervention_description: 20 minutes in a park or natural setting three times per week

title: Water Aerobics Helps Arthritis
headline: Water exercises reduce pain and improve function in arthritis
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 380 adults with knee osteoarthritis to either water aerobics or education classes for 12 weeks. Those doing water exercise had less pain and better knee function. Water reduces joint stress while allowing strengthening. Strong evidence for aquatic exercise in arthritis.
intervention_description: Twice-weekly 45-minute water aerobics classes

title: Green Tea Extract Aids Weight Loss
headline: Green tea extract modestly helps with weight loss
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 340 overweight adults to either green tea extract supplements or placebo for 12 weeks. Those taking green tea lost slightly more weight. The effect was modest but statistically significant. Green tea may boost metabolism slightly. This is moderate-strength evidence.
intervention_description: 500mg green tea extract capsule daily

title: Social Prescribing Improves Wellbeing
headline: Connecting lonely people with community activities improves health
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 420 adults with loneliness and mild health issues to either social prescribing or usual care for 6 months. Those connected to community groups had better wellbeing and fewer GP visits. Social connection is a legitimate health intervention. Strong evidence for social prescribing.
intervention_description: Link worker connecting patients to community activities and groups
conditions: Social isolation and mild health conditions

title: Standing Desks Reduce Sitting Time
headline: Standing desks significantly reduce daily sitting
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 290 office workers to either receive standing desks or continue with regular desks for 12 months. Those with standing desks sat 1.5 hours less per day and reported less back pain. Standing desks are an effective way to break up prolonged sitting. Strong evidence for workplace intervention.
intervention_description: Height-adjustable desk allowing standing while working

title: Reducing Added Sugar Improves Health Markers
headline: Cutting added sugar improves multiple health markers quickly
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 240 adults with high sugar intake to either reduce added sugars or maintain their usual diet for 9 days. Those cutting sugar showed improved triglycerides, LDL cholesterol, and blood pressure in just 9 days. Calories were kept the same. Strong evidence against added sugars.
intervention_description: Added sugars reduced from 28% to 10% of calories
population: ages 30 to 55 with high sugar intake

title: Gratitude Practice Improves Sleep
headline: Writing gratitude lists helps people sleep better
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 180 adults with poor sleep to either write three things they were grateful for before bed or write about neutral events for 4 weeks. The gratitude group fell asleep faster and slept longer. A simple free intervention with real benefits. Strong evidence for gratitude practice.
intervention_description: Writing three things to be grateful for before bed each night

title: Gardening Improves Mental Health
headline: Regular gardening reduces depression and anxiety
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 320 adults with mild mental health difficulties to either community gardening or a waiting list for 12 weeks. Gardeners showed significant improvements in depression and anxiety scores. Gardening combines physical activity, nature exposure, and purpose. Strong evidence for therapeutic gardening.
intervention_description: Weekly participation in community garden activities
population: ages 30 to 70 with mild anxiety or depression

title: Berries Improve Brain Function
headline: Eating berries daily improves memory in older adults
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 280 older adults with mild memory complaints to either eat blueberries daily or a placebo powder for 6 months. Berry eaters showed improved memory and thinking speed. Berries are high in flavonoids that may protect brain health. Strong evidence for berry consumption.
intervention_description: One cup of blueberries or equivalent berry supplement daily
population: ages 60 to 80 with mild memory concerns

title: Pet Ownership Reduces Blood Pressure
headline: Having a pet helps lower blood pressure
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 180 adults with high blood pressure to either adopt a pet or remain on a waiting list for 6 months. Pet owners had lower blood pressure readings. The companionship and routine care requirements both contribute. Strong evidence for pets and cardiovascular health.
intervention_description: Adopting a dog or cat from a shelter

title: Dance Classes Prevent Cognitive Decline
headline: Social dancing helps maintain cognitive function in older adults
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 420 older adults to either dance classes or traditional exercise for 18 months. Dancers showed better cognitive function. Dancing combines physical exercise, mental challenge, music, and social interaction. Strong evidence for dance as cognitive protection.
intervention_description: Twice-weekly 90-minute dance classes learning various styles

title: Olive Oil Reduces Heart Disease
headline: Extra virgin olive oil protects against heart disease
summary: In this large trial, researchers randomly assigned 740 adults at cardiovascular risk to either a Mediterranean diet with extra virgin olive oil or a low-fat diet for 5 years. The olive oil group had 30% fewer heart attacks and strokes. This was such strong evidence the trial was stopped early. Clear benefit for olive oil.
intervention_description: 4 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil daily as part of Mediterranean diet

title: Forest Bathing Reduces Cortisol
headline: Walking in forests lowers stress more than urban walking
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 180 adults with high stress to either forest walks or urban walks twice weekly for 8 weeks. Forest walkers had larger drops in cortisol and blood pressure. Even brief time in forests has measurable physiological benefits. Strong evidence for forest therapy.
intervention_description: 30-minute walks in forested areas twice weekly

title: Pickleball Improves Fitness in Older Adults
headline: Playing pickleball improves fitness and mood in seniors
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 260 sedentary older adults to either pickleball lessons or educational seminars for 12 weeks. Pickleball players had better fitness, lower blood pressure, and reported more social connection. It's accessible exercise that people actually enjoy. Strong evidence for recreational sports.
intervention_description: Twice-weekly 60-minute pickleball sessions with instruction

title: Reducing Processed Meat Lowers Cancer Risk
headline: Cutting processed meat reduces colorectal cancer risk markers
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 320 adults who eat processed meat daily to either eliminate it or continue their usual diet for 12 weeks. Those who stopped eating processed meat had lower markers associated with colorectal cancer risk. The WHO classifies processed meat as carcinogenic. Strong evidence to limit it.
intervention_description: No bacon sausage hot dogs or deli meats for 12 weeks
population: ages 40 to 70 regular processed meat consumers
